scope: Primary-source research supporting a compact passenger-coach brake feasibility study. No replacement brake CAD, purchased component selection, braking performance approval or manufacturing release is claimed.

project_basis.source: Root task and current C5 project geometry; project inputs, not manufacturer data.

conclusion.status: FEASIBILITY RESEARCH; NO VERIFIED 600 MM OEM COMPONENT FIT
conclusion.recommendation_class: Engineering inference and development recommendation, not manufacturer approval.
conclusion.recommendation: Develop a custom bogie-contained tread-block and rigging packaging study as a potential replacement for the present outboard drum/stub arrangement. Retain an inboard-disc alternative if tread-wheel thermal compatibility, shoe tracking or rigging clearances cannot be resolved.
conclusion.commercial_component_status: No public dimensioned general arrangement, mounting-hole drawing or STEP model was verified for a commercial tread-brake unit fitting the complete 600 mm wheel / 914.4 mm gauge / 1200 mm wheelbase combination. This is a limit of the retrieved evidence, not a claim that manufacturers cannot supply a suitable custom variant.
do_not_claim: That a TreadAct, BFC/BFCF, BFC G4, BFCB or IBB10 catalog unit fits the coach.
That maximum catalog block force is an appropriate operating setting for this coach.
That wear-adjuster stroke establishes permissible suspension movement.
That a simple pressure-to-apply air circuit automatically brakes after a severed supply hose.
That a service-air application alone provides indefinite parking security.
That the existing custom wheel blank is qualified for tread-brake thermal and contact duty.

facts: TreadAct Compact combines an air-powered brake cylinder, transmission mechanism and automatic slack adjuster.
The brochure identifies rigid and flexible PEC7 designs; the flexible illustration is described for high lateral axle movements.
Options include spring-operated, pneumatically released parking and hand-operated parking.
The brochure permits superposition of brake forces in failure cases for the described product family. This is not a generic permission for other equipment.

source_facts.locator: IREE 2023 Transit Tread Brake Unit sheet, page 1.
facts: The sheet identifies BFC and BFCF service/parking configurations, integrated slack adjustment, an anti-compound valve and a retention device.
Flexible units accommodate increased lateral wheel dynamics; no numerical movement limit is supplied.
The listed block/holder interfaces are UIC 250 and 320. These labels do not establish compatibility with a 600 mm wheel.
source_facts.exact_fit_limit: The published suitable-wheel range is 860-1250 mm; the project wheel is 600 mm and is outside that published range. No smaller custom variant is verified here.

source_facts.locator: BFCB Push Bogie Brake System datasheet, pages 1-2.
facts: Pneumatically actuated BFC spindles move primary and secondary beams apart, applying blocks to the bogie wheels.
A block-holder friction device maintains its position relative to the wheel despite wear and vibration; integrated slack adjustment maintains the released gap as wear occurs.
Hand and automatic parking options are described. Product specifications are explicitly application-dependent.
The retrieved current manufacturer PDF contains product illustrations, not a usable dimensioned mounting drawing.
source_facts.qualification: Marketing statements about adapting to gauges and bogie types do not establish this coach's fit.

source_facts.locator: UIC Freight Components PDF, Compact Brake Family pages 3-5; numerical table on page 4.
source_facts.exact_fit_limit: The gauge table begins at 1000 mm; the project gauge is 914.4 mm. The table supplies no verified 914.4 mm variant or mounting envelope.
source_facts.catalog_variation: The standalone BFCB sheet S3 gives 250 kg for its hand-brake example; family table S4 gives 255 kg. These are source-specific catalog examples, not a frozen mass for the proposed coach installation.

source_facts.locator: Knorr-Bremse-authored patent EP0665153B1, Figures 1-2 and associated description.
facts: A bracket fastened to the bogie frame carries a pivoted brake unit, hanging link and parallel guide.
An articulated coupling near axle height joins the assembly to the adjacent outer axlebox.
The arrangement is intended to preserve block alignment and clearance while accommodating wheelset movement.
source_facts.qualification: This is an original mechanical disclosure used as an architecture reference. It is not a current product installation drawing, performance validation or proof of fit. No patent/legal status conclusion is made.

facts: Knorr describes purely pneumatic indirect braking via brake pipe and distributor valve, and direct electro-pneumatic architectures.
Control may be organized per coach or per bogie, with load-dependent pressure functions and optional wheel-slide protection.
Direct electro-pneumatic braking in a complete railway control architecture is not equivalent to an unprotected simple pressure-to-apply hose circuit.
source_facts.qualification: The last distinction is an engineering interpretation of the architectures, not a claim that the cited control products have been selected for this train.

facts: The TSB technical background describes brake pipe, car control valve, auxiliary/emergency reservoirs and brake cylinders as elements of the automatic air-brake system.
A sufficient brake-pipe pressure reduction causes each control valve to send stored local reservoir air to its brake cylinder.
source_facts.evidence_limit: The official page's indexed primary-source text was retrieved; a subsequent full-page request returned HTTP 403. This record uses only the supported system description, not unviewed numerical limits.

facts: The TSB's Field investigation found that air leakage after a prolonged stationary period reduced brake holding force sufficiently for the train to move on the grade.
source_facts.qualification: An observed failure mechanism, not a transfer of that freight train's grade, timing, legal requirements or quantitative performance to this project.

facts: Knorr describes wheel-slide protection as preventing wheelset locking when wheel-rail adhesion deteriorates during braking.
source_facts.qualification: No wheel-slide protection hardware or achieved stopping distance is selected or validated for this train.

facts: Wabtec markets BFC G4 as a compact bogie-mounted tread-brake unit.

engineering_inferences_and_requirements.statement: The block should engage the running tread around the wheel circumference. The proposed wheel profile, flange exclusion, block curvature/width, material pairing, new/worn radii and replacement access must be resolved together; a block touching the blank wheel in CAD is not qualified tread contact.

Near a front/rear contact at axle height, block normal force N is predominantly horizontal and friction force mu_block*N is predominantly vertical. Bracket/hanger/guide loads and wheel-load transfer therefore need explicit free-body analysis. They cannot be sized from the longitudinal train stopping force alone.

idealized_relations.single_block_torque_Nm_at_nominal_radius: T = 0.300 * mu_block * N, with N in newtons
idealized_relations.separate_adhesion_limit: Wheel-rail braking force is limited by wheel-rail adhesion and instantaneous wheel load; mu_block is not mu_rail.

engineering_inferences_and_requirements.qualification: Friction coefficient, actual contact angle, load sharing and compliance are unselected. Opposing clasp blocks can partly balance reaction components only when their force distribution is demonstrated.

engineering_inferences_and_requirements.statement: Provide explicit shoe/beam mobility and reaction support through the frozen full axle-to-frame travel, crosslevel, axle tilt and lateral clearance. Wear adjustment is not suspension tracking. Include released and applied states, wheel/block wear, tolerances and service access. No numeric movement capability is inferred from actuator stroke.

Study a train-wide automatic brake-pipe system with protected local coach air storage and a specified service/emergency control function. A basic direct pressure-to-apply circuit loses its command/energy when its hose ruptures unless a separate engineered emergency function is provided. Direct EP systems can include such functions; direct EP must not be categorically described as unsafe.
still_required: Pressure and timing at the last coach

engineering_inferences_and_requirements.statement: Specify a mechanical holding function using a suitable spring parking or hand-brake arrangement; do not credit retained service pressure indefinitely. The selected system must define service/parking compounding behavior, release indication and manual recovery release. Catalog spring force is not a train-on-grade holding calculation.

basis: Energy balance and proposed contact architecture
engineering_inferences_and_requirements.statement: Check stop energy, repeated stops and continuous downgrade energy against the wheel/block friction pair. Low speed alone does not prove acceptable thermal duty. For a candidate duty cycle, include kinetic energy change and gravitational energy on descent; allocation among wheels and any locomotive retardation must be explicit.

Bound the effects of worn-out adjustment travel, seized or broken rigging, dragging or missing blocks, air leakage, low adhesion, unintended parking/service compounding and any released recovery device. Define retention of detached rigging so it cannot drop into the track envelope.

minimum_component_interface_package_befo: Selected variant's dimensioned general arrangement or verified CAD, including ports and service access.
600 mm new-wheel and minimum worn-wheel compatibility with the actual wheel tread and block geometry.
Mounting reactions, hardware specifications and permitted attachment stiffness/deflection.
Permitted vertical, lateral and angular movements in applied and released states.
Force versus pressure/stroke, wear-adjustment capacity and released clearance.
Parking force, release pressure, anti-compounding or permitted simultaneous-force behavior and manual release details.
Friction/thermal duty, maintenance and replacement data for the selected wheel/block pair.
